correctness.rationale: Exact directed error balls yield six-neighbor triangular confusability for every n>=2, including boundaries. Residue i+2j mod 3 gives pairwise-disjoint error images. The explicit three-row partition into m disjoint triangles, an edge and a singleton bounds an independent set by m+2; color 2 meets it for all m. Exact bases at n=2,3,4 and recurrence M(n)=M(n-3)+n-1 imply floor(n(n+1)/6). Standalone verifier checks direct error images through length 50, partitions through m=150, and independently computes exact finite maxima n=2..9. Infinite theorem rests on proof, not experiments.

originality.rationale: Research-record searches, comparison with accessible preceding claims, and material inspection of primary literature found no source whose theorem or stronger parameters imply the exact one-direction, at-most-one-swap, weight-two capacity floor(n(n+1)/6) for every n and a matching three-row clique partition. The closest weight-two packing theorem treats both directions and differs already at n=4. The 2023 direction-specific coding paper proves general redundancy guarantees instead. Limited access to Kløve 1995 remains a priority risk and search absence is not an absolute novelty certificate.

value.rationale: Directional peak-shift correction is a motivated error channel; exact optimal zero-error capacity for every length in the weight-two layer is not supplied by published bidirectional two-token bounds. The all-n sharp clique-packing technique, transparent residue code and constant-size candidate decoder are mathematically and operationally useful; it is neither a narrow arbitrary numeric slice nor a straightforward corollary of a stronger known optimum.
